open_obligations: Check that Kenton et al. actually make the remark attributed to them about consultancy being a weak baseline
Check whether the authors' own result that Consultancy underperforms NaiveJudge on ASD bears on the same point
out.other_title: Assigned-role consultancy and debate with an LLM judge, compared with direct QA baselines
out.rationale: The authors say that previous debate experiments used Random Consultancy as a baseline and, citing Kenton et al. (2024), that this is still a weak baseline: debate beating it is only a 'sufficing' result that does not help the goal of comparing across protocols. The target passage presents the comparison between consultancy and debate as an empirical test of whether debate can enable more accurate judgment and does not itself contain the weak-baseline remark, so the source shows a limit of that comparison. This is an argument rather than an empirical result.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: Whether assigned-role (random) consultancy is an adequate baseline for judging debate's benefit.

text: The authors say previous debate experiments used Random Consultancy as a baseline and, as Kenton et al. (2024) note, this is still a weak baseline: debate beating it amounts to hearing both sides being better than hearing only the wrong side half the time. They conclude it is only a sufficing result that does not help compare protocols.
title: Sudhir et al. agree with Kenton et al. that random consultancy is a weak baseline for debate
